taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

September 30, 2026, falls during Daylight Saving Time for both regions. Madrid is in Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2), and the Eastern Time zone is in Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4). The time difference is 6 hours.

Adding 6 hours to 5:00 PM (17:00) ET results in 11:00 PM (23:00) in Madrid on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru, is in the Peru Time (PET) zone, which is UTC-5. To find the local time, subtract 5 hours from 12:00 UTC.

12:00 - 5 hours = 07:00.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST (Central European Summer Time) is UTC+2, and Tokyo (JST) is UTC+9. Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST. Adding 7 hours to 9:00 AM on June 1, 2026, results in 4:00 PM (16:00) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) is UTC-7. Madrid, Spain, follows CEST (Central European Summer Time) in October, which is UTC+2. The time difference is 9 hours.

Adding 9 hours to October 11, 2026, at 11:59 PM results in October 12, 2026, at 8:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is March 3, 2026, at 11:59 PM PST. 

1. **Time Zone Offset**: PST (Pacific Standard Time) is UTC-8. Madrid, Spain, in March operates on CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1.
2. **Time Difference**: Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PST (1 - (-8) = 9).
3. **Calculation**: Adding 9 hours to March 3 at 23:59 results in March 4 at 08:59.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1, and Los Angeles (Pacific Standard Time) is UTC-8 in February. This means Los Angeles is 9 hours behind CET.

10:00 AM CET minus 9 hours is 1:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9, and Lima, Peru (PET) is UTC-5. This means JST is 14 hours ahead of Lima.

Subtracting 14 hours from May 5, 2026, at 8:00 AM:
- 8 hours back takes us to 12:00 AM (midnight) on May 5.
- 6 more hours back takes us to 6:00 PM (18:00) on May 4.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 28, 2026, Pacific Time (PT) is still in Daylight Saving Time (PDT, UTC-7), as the US transition occurs on November 1. Spain transitions from CEST to CET (UTC+1) on October 25, 2026. Therefore, on October 28, Madrid is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time.

11:59 PM PT on October 28 + 8 hours = 7:59 AM on October 29.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 30, 2026, the United States will still be observing Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. Spain ends its Daylight Saving Time on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026), so by October 30, Madrid will be observing Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.

The time difference between UTC-4 and UTC+1 is 5 hours.
9:00 AM ET + 5 hours = 2:00 PM (14:00) local time in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1. On October 27, 2026, New York will still be observing EDT (Eastern Daylight Time), which is UTC-4. The time difference is 5 hours (CET is 5 hours ahead of EDT).

18:00 - 5 hours = 13:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On November 2, 2026, both locations will have transitioned out of Daylight Saving Time. The US (Pacific Time) will be on PST (UTC-8) as of November 1, and Spain (Madrid) will be on CET (UTC+1) as of October 25. 

The time difference between PST (UTC-8) and CET (UTC+1) is 9 hours. Adding 9 hours to November 2, 11:59 PM PT results in November 3, 8:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 20, 2026, the US will have already started Daylight Saving Time (beginning March 8), meaning PT will be PDT (UTC-7). However, Spain will not yet have started Daylight Saving Time (beginning March 29), meaning Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1). 

The time difference between UTC-7 and UTC+1 is 8 hours. Adding 8 hours to March 20 at 11:59 PM results in March 21 at 7:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 25, 2026, Central European Time (CET) is UTC+1. Los Angeles will be observing Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. The time difference is 8 hours. Subtracting 8 hours from 12:00 PM CET results in 4:00 AM PDT.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is 12:00 AM ET (Eastern Time) on October 12, 2026. On this date, the US is in Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) and Madrid is in Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2).

The time difference is 6 hours (Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET). Adding 6 hours to 12:00 AM on October 12 results in 6:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

"Anywhere on Earth" (AoE) corresponds to the time zone UTC-12. To find the deadline in Madrid, Spain, we calculate the difference between UTC-12 and Madrid's local time.

1.  **AoE to UTC**: AoE is 12 hours behind UTC. Therefore, October 9, 23:59 AoE is October 10, 11:59 UTC.
2.  **UTC to Madrid**: In October, Madrid is on Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. Adding 2 hours to 11:59 UTC on October 10 results in 13:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In August, Pacific Time (PT) is in Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. Madrid, Spain, is in Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. The time difference is 9 hours (Madrid is ahead).

12:00 PM (noon) PT + 9 hours = 9:00 PM (21:00) local time in Madrid on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST (India Standard Time) is UTC+5:30. Madrid, Spain, in November is on CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1. The time difference is 4 hours and 30 minutes (IST is ahead of CET).

Subtracting 4 hours and 30 minutes from 11:59 PM (23:59) on November 10, 2026, results in 7:29 PM (19:29) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Standard Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45, and Peru Time (PET) is UTC-5. This means Nepal is 10 hours and 45 minutes ahead of Lima.

Subtracting 10 hours and 45 minutes from April 2, 2026, at 5:00 PM (17:00):
- 17:00 minus 10 hours is 07:00.
- 07:00 minus 45 minutes is 06:15.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 6, 2026, Adelaide will be observing Australian Central Daylight Time (ACDT), which is UTC+10:30. Madrid will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

The time difference is 8 hours and 30 minutes (10.5 - 2 = 8.5). To find the local time in Madrid, subtract 8 hours and 30 minutes from 10:00 AM.

10:00 - 8 hours = 02:00
02:00 - 30 minutes = 01:30

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is on Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST, UTC+10) on October 3, 2026, as daylight saving time does not begin until the following day (Sunday, October 4). Madrid is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) in early October. The time difference is 8 hours (Sydney is ahead of Madrid).

Subtracting 8 hours from 6:00 PM (18:00) Sydney time results in 10:00 AM Madrid time on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
